items.title: Live: Khamenei's son named as Iran's new supreme leader, state media reports
items.description: Mojtaba Khamenei will replace his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as the country's new supreme leader, state media has reported. Follow live.

items.title: Tough talk and video games: How the war is being sold to Americans
items.description: The US administration's unapologetic stance on the war has come with a lot of bravado, but there are signs the American public is not convinced.

items.title: Water supply gets cut, then things get complicated. Here's today's quick scan on Iran
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and will provide daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Oil markets are getting the war in the Middle East all wrong
items.description: Investors seem calm, relying on Donald Trump's reputation as a deal maker but the reality is this conflict could be long and destabilising.

items.title: Live: ASX plunges 4pc, on track for worst sell-off since Trump tariffs
items.description: The All Ordinaries has shed 4pc, or about $120 billion in value, as global markets crumble and oil prices surge15pc towards $US110/barrel. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Deirdre has cared for her son for 45 years. He'll soon enter the unknown
items.description: Deirdre Croft has dedicated 45 years to caring and advocating for her intellectually disabled son, Richard. Each passing day brings more pressure to secure his future when she's gone.

items.title: Live: Government won't say which Gulf state requested Australia's military assistance
items.description: The government is currently considering a request to provide military assistance to a Gulf nation, but it won't say which one. Follow live.

items.title: 'Let them go': Chaos erupts as protesters surround Iran team bus on Gold Coast
items.description: Protesters surround the Iranian women's football team bus after their final match in the Asian Cup, as fears grow for their safety.

items.title: Frustrated Matildas exposed by South Korea but prepared for the long road at Asian Cup
items.description: In the moments that mattered, the Matildas lacked composure, while South Korea made them pay. They'll now have to do it the hard way if they're going to go all the way at the Women's Asian Cup.

items.title: Defiant and proud — Australian Jews speak out in first ABC National Forum
items.description: Along with authors, teachers, students, parents and grandparents, Kahn will tell her story of life in Australia as a Jew in the first ABC National Forum.

items.title: Australian business owners in Dubai 'staying put'
items.description: Escalating geopolitical tensions mean Australians operating businesses in the Middle East have had to make quick changes to their daily operations.

items.title: Supply lines open after food shortage, amid major Katherine flooding
items.description: While Katherine remains under an emergency flood warning, water levels are now receding and food supply lines are opening up.

items.title: F1 fans have seen the new era in all its chaotic and thrilling glory
items.description: Formula 1's new era began with a dramatic, chaotic, and compelling grand prix in Melbourne. While views on the regulations are mixed, fans will likely be the ones to decide if it is a success or failure.

items.title: The world has changed since 2003 and so has Anthony Albanese
items.description: The Albanese government will need to be explicit about what it is doing in the Middle East or risk a growing concern that it is being drawn into another war.

items.title: A career break gave one woman a 'safety net' to return to her job
items.description: Whether it’s for a holiday, additional study or a exploring a new field of work, experts say a career break can have many benefits.

items.title: Thirty years ago, Bridget Jones paved the way for future comic heroines
items.description: When Oxford-educated Helen Fielding introduced readers to Bridget Jones in her newspaper column, in her own words, she was "quite embarrassed". Three decades later, the book has sold more than 15 million copies worldwide.

items.title: 'Shell shocked': From being lost in motherhood to Muster Dogs champion
items.description: After swapping corporate city life for her family's remote seventh-generation farm, Courtney Moir has claimed the top spot in this year's season of Muster Dogs.

items.title: Tourists to be slugged new tax to visit Twelve Apostles on Great Ocean Road
items.description: The amount tourists will be charged to visit the Twelve Apostles is subject to consultation with stakeholders.

items.title: People doing EMDR mental health therapy warned they may lose legal justice
items.description: Katie Bird sought psychological help for intrusive memories related to alleged sexual abuse. Her court case was discontinued because she underwent eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy.

items.title: Road linking Sydney to western NSW shut by damage to 194yo bridge
items.description: The Great Western Highway between Lithgow and Mount Victoria is closed due to damage being found in a historic bridge.

items.title: Crime gangs use fake plain packaging from China to flood Australian market
items.description: Australian crime syndicates are using fake plain packaging — mass produced overseas — to legitimise illicit tobacco and flood the legal market with knock-offs.

items.title: Camper dies in alleged stabbing during dispute at campsite
items.description: Police allege an altercation between two men has ended in a fatal stabbing at a campsite near Tamworth.

items.title: Aussie overcomes dislocated shoulder to claim silver at Winter Paralympics
items.description: Ben Tudhope wins silver in the snowboard cross to register Australia's first medal at the 2026 Winter Paralympics.

items.title: India crushes New Zealand in T20 World Cup final to claim back-to-back titles
items.description: India is sent in to bat in the T20 World Cup final and dominates from start to finish to claim its third title.

items.title: Australia falls just short of stunning victory over Japan at World Baseball Classic
items.description: Australia pushes baseball juggernauts Japan all the way in their World Baseball Classic clash.
